category.name: Knowledge and research data
category.description: Encyclopedias, academic papers, news, computational knowledge and up-to-date library documentation.

entries.name: arXiv API
entries.desc_en: Search arXiv preprints by keyword, author, category or ID and retrieve metadata, abstracts and PDF links.
entries.notes: Endpoint: http://export.arxiv.org/api/query, returns Atom XML. Terms of Use allow no more than one request every three seconds over a single connection. For bulk harvesting use OAI-PMH or bulk data instead.

entries.name: Congress.gov API
entries.auth_hint: api.data.gov key: query parameter ?api_key=<API_KEY> or header X-Api-Key: <API_KEY>
entries.free_tier: Free: government API, key issued instantly by email; 5,000 requests/hour.
entries.desc_en: Lets an agent look up U.S. bills, amendments, votes, members, committees, nominations and Congressional Record data from the Library of Congress.
entries.notes: Official Library of Congress API (v3); usage guide and endpoint docs in github.com/LibraryOfCongress/api.congress.gov. Paginated JSON/XML, max 250 results per page.

entries.name: Context7 (library docs for agents)
entries.auth_hint: Authorization: Bearer <ctx7sk_... key> (optional; works at low limits without key)
entries.free_tier: free; low limits without key, free API key from context7.com/dashboard raises limits
entries.desc_en: Fetch up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples into a coding agent's context via MCP or REST.
entries.notes: Maintained by Upstash; repo https://github.com/upstash/context7. Local server @upstash/context7-mcp, also a ctx7 CLI and @upstash/context7-sdk. REST base URL: https://context7.com/api/. Exceeding the limit returns 429 with Retry-After/RateLimit-* headers. Paid plans cover teams and private repos.

entries.name: Crossref REST API
entries.auth_hint: no key; add mailto=<email> param or User-Agent contact for the 'polite pool'
entries.desc_en: Look up and search scholarly metadata such as DOIs, references, authors, funders and licenses across Crossref-registered works.
entries.notes: Base URL https://api.crossref.org (/works, /journals, /funders, /members). Rate limits are adaptive, reported in X-Rate-Limit-Limit/X-Rate-Limit-Interval headers. Identify yourself with mailto for better service. Metadata Plus is a paid SLA tier.

entries.name: GDELT API
entries.desc_en: Full-text search global news in about 65 languages and analyze coverage volume, tone and geography in near real time.
entries.notes: DOC 2.0 API: https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc. Covers a rolling window of about 3 months, max 250 records per query. GEO 2.0 and TV APIs also exist. Full historical Events/GKG data available via Google BigQuery (needs a billed Google Cloud account).

entries.name: Gitingest API
entries.auth_hint: No key for public repos: GET https://gitingest.com/api/<owner>/<repo>; optional GitHub token for private repos via the 'token' parameter
entries.free_tier: No key; free public service with no published quota (the web UI has rate limiting and CAPTCHA protection).
entries.desc_en: Lets an agent turn any public Git repository into a single text digest (summary, directory tree and file contents) sized for an LLM prompt.
entries.notes: GET /api/{user}/{repo} or POST /api/ingest (include/exclude patterns); digest returned as a download URL. For heavy use the vendor recommends the open-source CLI (pip install gitingest).

entries.name: Hacker News API
entries.desc_en: Read Hacker News stories, comments, jobs, polls, user profiles and front-page rankings as real-time JSON.
entries.notes: Base URL https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/. Read-only, no documented rate limit. No full-text search; use the separate Algolia HN Search API for that.

entries.name: Internet Archive Open Library API
entries.auth_hint: No key; send a User-Agent header with app name and contact email, e.g. 'User-Agent: MyApp (me@example.org)'
entries.free_tier: No key; free and open: 1 request/second anonymous, 3 requests/second with an identifying User-Agent.
entries.desc_en: Lets an agent search books, authors and subjects, fetch work/edition data by ISBN or OLID, search inside book texts and get cover images.
entries.notes: Bulk scraping discouraged; use the monthly data dumps for large jobs. Reading-log/list write endpoints need an Open Library login.

entries.name: New York Times APIs
entries.auth_hint: Query parameter ?api-key=<API_KEY> (create an app at developer.nytimes.com and enable the APIs you need)
entries.free_tier: Free: all public APIs are free; most APIs 500 requests/day and 5 requests/minute (Archive API higher).
entries.desc_en: Lets an agent search NYT articles back to 1851, read top stories, most-popular lists, the Times Wire feed and bestseller lists.
entries.notes: Returns metadata/abstracts and links, not full article text. Exceeding limits returns HTTP 429; wait ~12 s between calls. Non-commercial use terms.

entries.name: NewsAPI
entries.auth_hint: X-Api-Key: <key> header or apiKey=<key> query param
entries.free_tier: free Developer plan: 100 req/day, dev/test only, 24h article delay
entries.desc_en: Search and retrieve current and historical news articles and top headlines from thousands of sources worldwide.
entries.notes: Free plan is barred from staging/production, including internal use; CORS allowed from localhost only. Production use needs the Business plan ($449/mo, 250k req/mo). Endpoints: /v2/everything, /v2/top-headlines.

entries.name: OpenAlex API
entries.auth_hint: api_key=<key> query param (optional; basic use works without key)
entries.free_tier: free: $1 of API usage/day without payment method; free key raises daily budget 10x
entries.desc_en: Query an open catalog of scholarly works, authors, institutions, sources and topics, including citation data, via REST.
entries.notes: Base URL https://api.openalex.org. docs.openalex.org now redirects to help.openalex.org. Free daily budget resets at midnight UTC; above it, pay-as-you-go with prepaid $1 increments. Annual Member plans start at $5,000/yr. Data is CC0.

entries.name: PubMed E-utilities (NCBI)
entries.auth_hint: optional api_key=<NCBI key> query param; tool and email params recommended
entries.free_tier: free; 3 req/s without key, 10 req/s with free NCBI API key
entries.desc_en: Search, fetch, summarize and cross-link biomedical literature records from PubMed, PMC and other Entrez databases.
entries.notes: Base URL https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/ (esearch, efetch, esummary, elink). Free API key from NCBI account settings. Run heavy jobs off-peak.

entries.name: Semantic Scholar API
entries.free_tier: free; no key (shared, throttled pool) or free API key on request
entries.desc_en: Search papers, authors and citation graphs, and get paper recommendations from Semantic Scholar's academic corpus.
entries.notes: Without a key, all users share a pool of 1000 req/s that can be throttled under load. A key starts at 1 req/s dedicated; requested via web form, arrives by email (not instant). Three APIs: Academic Graph, Recommendations, Datasets.

entries.name: Wikidata
entries.auth_hint: no auth for reads (descriptive User-Agent required); OAuth2 Bearer only for edits
entries.desc_en: Query the Wikidata knowledge graph of entities, facts and relations via SPARQL, the REST API or MCP.
entries.notes: Official MCP comes from Wikimedia Deutschland (github.com/wmde/WikidataMCP). SPARQL endpoint: https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, query timeout ~60s. REST API at /w/rest.php/wikibase/v1. Wikimedia rate limits and User-Agent policy apply. Added because it's a widely-used structured-knowledge source missing from the candidate list.

entries.name: Wikipedia / Wikimedia API
entries.auth_hint: Reads need no key but require a descriptive User-Agent header with contact info. Optional OAuth2 via Authorization: Bearer <access token> raises rate limits.
entries.desc_en: Search, read and summarize Wikipedia and other Wikimedia content and metadata via REST and Action APIs.
entries.notes: The old API Portal at api.wikimedia.org now 301-redirects to mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_APIs. Documented limits: 10 req/min for requests identified only by IP, 200 req/min for unauthenticated requests with a proper User-Agent, 2000 req/min for established editors. Main endpoints are the per-wiki MediaWiki Action API (/w/api.php) and REST APIs.

entries.name: Wolfram|Alpha API
entries.auth_hint: appid=<AppID> query param or Authorization: Bearer <AppID>
entries.free_tier: free non-commercial developer AppID (reported up to 2,000 calls/month); paid for commercial use
entries.desc_en: Get computed answers, structured data and step-by-step results for math, science and factual queries.
entries.notes: LLM API endpoint https://www.wolframalpha.com/api/v1/llm-api is built for agents; output length set by maxchars (default 6800). Get an AppID via the Developer Portal. Other APIs: Full Results, Simple, Short Answers, Spoken Results. Commercial use requires a paid license. The official MCP is the Wolfram Cloud MCP, covering Wolfram technology broadly.
